draft.title: Erosion and deposition
card: the wearing away and carrying off of rock and soil by water, wind, waves and ice. Moving agents scrape, hit and carry material away from where it was.
the movement of eroded pieces from one place to another. Rivers, wind, waves and glaciers all carry material.
the dropping of material when the agent slows down or loses energy. This builds landforms such as beaches, sand dunes and deltas.
A delta forms where a river slows as it meets the sea or a lake and drops its load. Waves also erode coasts. They wear away the base of a cliff, so the cliff retreats.
draft.remember: Erosion takes material away. Deposition drops it and builds landforms such as beaches and deltas.

a.q: A river carries mud and sand to the sea. It slows and drops the load, building a fan of new land at its mouth. Which process built it?
opts: Wearing away of the river bank
a.why: The river slowed and lost energy, so it dropped its load. Dropping material builds land, and a delta forms this way. Erosion takes material away, so it does not build a delta.
a.clue: What happened to the sand and mud when the river slowed?

b.q: Waves hit the base of a sea cliff for many years. The cliff slowly moves back and loses rock. Which process is mainly at work?
opts: Building of a delta by a river
b.why: Waves wear away the base of the cliff and carry the rock off, so the cliff retreats. Deposition, beaches and deltas all add material, so they do not make a cliff retreat.
b.clue: Was material taken away or added?
